title: Finite Galois envelopes after Tate normalization
statement: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], complete for a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. Let $C\ne0$ be a reduced quotient of a restricted-series ring [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation] with a Tate quotient Banach norm. There exist an integer $s\ge1$, nonzero normal affinoid domains $B_1,\ldots,B_s$, maps $j_i:C\to B_i$, and injective maps $T_i=K\langle U_1,\ldots,U_{d_i}\rangle\hookrightarrow B_i$ ($d_i\ge0$), with the following properties. Each $B_i$ is a finitely generated $C$-module through $j_i$ and a finitely generated $T_i$-module. The map $j=(j_1,\ldots,j_s):C\to\prod_i B_i$ is injective. Each $T_i$ is an integrally closed domain, and the extension $\operatorname{Frac}(B_i)/\operatorname{Frac}(T_i)$ is finite Galois (finite, separable and normal). Here normal domain means integrally closed in its fraction field. Each $B_i$ admits a Tate quotient Banach norm $\|\cdot\|_i$ for which both structure maps are bounded: there are positive real constants $D_i,E_i$ with $\|j_i(c)\|_i\le D_i\|c\|_C$ and $\|t\|_i\le E_i\|t\|_G$ for all $c\in C,t\in T_i$.

source.place: More on affinoid algebras, proof of Theorem 4, PDF p.2: minimal-prime decomposition, Noether normalization and normal closure; stages (a),(b). Read online 2026-10-24. Corrected algebraic preparation over algebraically closed K: absorb the bounded purely inseparable part into a Tate algebra with p-power-root variables before taking the separable normal closure. This is an algebraic envelope assertion, not the spectral-completeness conclusion. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The presentation ring is Noetherian by lem-trf-affinoid-polynomial-closed-point-comparison, applied with $J=0$, so that the quotient algebra there is the restricted-series ring itself. Its quotient $C$ is module finite (generated by $1$), so lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian makes $C$ Noetherian. By lem-sc-finite-minimal-primes-over-ideal, its minimal primes form a finite list $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_s$. By lem-per-nilradical-minimal-prime-intersection their intersection is the nilradical, hence zero because $C$ is reduced. The list is nonempty: an empty intersection is $C$, and $C\ne0$. Thus $s\ge1$, each $A_i=C/\mathfrak p_i$ is a nonzero domain and a quotient of the original series ring, and $C\to\prod_i A_i$ has zero kernel.

source.place: Theorem 4 proof, PDF p.2, first paragraph; algebraic minimal-prime reduction.

proof.text: Apply lem-trf-tate-normalization-lift to the proper kernel of the composite presentation onto each $A_i$. It supplies an injective map $S_i=K\langle X_1,\ldots,X_{d_i}\rangle\hookrightarrow A_i$ with $A_i$ finite over $S_i$. By lem-trf-finite-domain-fraction-degree the extension $L_i=\operatorname{Frac}(A_i)$ over $F_i=\operatorname{Frac}(S_i)$ is finite. By lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral every element of $A_i$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $S_i$. These are algebraic assertions and require no spectral norm completeness.

source.place: Theorem 4 proof, PDF p.2, reduction to a finite extension of a Tate algebra.

proof.text: Apply lem-trf-tate-variable-roots-separable-compositum to $L_i/F_i$. In its common algebraic overfield write $T_i=(S_i)_{q_i}$, $F_i^\prime=\operatorname{Frac}(T_i)$, and $M_i=L_iF_i^\prime$. Then $S_i\hookrightarrow T_i$ is finite free and $M_i/F_i^\prime$ is finite separable. In characteristic zero this uses $q_i=1$; in characteristic $p$ it uses a sufficiently large finite $p$-power, rather than assuming $F_i$ perfect. Regard $A_i$ as a subring of $M_i$ via $A_i\subseteq L_i$.

source.place: Theorem 4 proof, PDF p.2, part (a), root-variable preparation; the compositum formulation is the agent clarification in the cited node.

proof.text: Apply lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-receiving-separable-extensions to the one-element family $M_i/F_i^\prime$. It gives a finite Galois extension $N_i/F_i^\prime$ and an $F_i^\prime$-embedding $M_i\hookrightarrow N_i$. Transport the inclusion of $A_i$ along this embedding. Let $B_i$ be the integral closure of $T_i$ in $N_i$: by definition it is the subring of elements of $N_i$ satisfying a monic polynomial over $T_i$. Each element of $A_i$ lies in $B_i$, since the monic relation over $S_i$ from step 2 is still a monic relation over $T_i$. This gives an injective $A_i\hookrightarrow B_i$ and hence $j_i:C\twoheadrightarrow A_i\hookrightarrow B_i$.

source.place: Theorem 4 proof, PDF p.2, integral closure in a normal closure, after the inseparable preparation.

proof.text: The algebra $T_i$ is a domain integrally closed in its fraction field, i.e. a normal domain, by lem-trf-tate-integrally-closed, and Noetherian by lem-trf-affinoid-polynomial-closed-point-comparison with $J=0$. The extension $N_i/\operatorname{Frac}(T_i)$ is finite separable, so lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-normal-separable-integral-closure-finite (Stacks 032L) makes $B_i$ a finite $T_i$-module. By lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal it is a nonzero normal domain and its fraction field is $N_i$, through the actual inclusion. Thus $\operatorname{Frac}(B_i)/\operatorname{Frac}(T_i)$ is finite Galois, with the structural map specified in step 4.

source.place: Tag 032L, lemma-Noetherian-normal-domain-finite-separable-extension; Tag 034L, lemma-integral-closure-in-normal, and the cited fraction-field node.

proof.text: Choose finite $S_i$-module generators $u_a$ of $T_i$ from step 3 and finite $T_i$-module generators $v_b$ of $B_i$ from step 5. Their products $u_av_b$ generate $B_i$ over $S_i$: expand a coefficient of each $v_b$ in the $u_a$. The same family generates over $A_i$, since $S_i\subseteq A_i\subseteq B_i$, and over $C$ through its surjection to $A_i$, since every $A_i$-coefficient lifts to $C$. Finally, $j_i(c)=0$ implies $c\in\mathfrak p_i$ by injectivity of $A_i\to B_i$. Hence $j(c)=0$ implies $c\in\bigcap_i\mathfrak p_i=0$. This proves the required $C$-finiteness and joint injectivity without asserting that an individual $j_i$ is injective.

source.place: Theorem 4 proof, PDF p.2, finite-component envelope assembly; finite-generator calculation.

proof.text: Apply lem-trf-finite-algebra-affinoid-presentation to the finite algebra $T_i\hookrightarrow B_i$. It equips $B_i$ with a Tate quotient Banach norm. Both $C$ and $T_i$ already have such norms, the latter its Gauss norm from the identity presentation. Apply lem-trf-affinoid-homomorphism-bounded separately to the unital $K$-algebra maps $j_i:C\to B_i$ and $T_i\hookrightarrow B_i$. It gives positive real $D_i,E_i$ with $\|j_i(c)\|_i\le D_i\|c\|_C$ and $\|t\|_i\le E_i\|t\|_G$. All requested objects and inequalities now hold, including $d_i=0$ when normalization has zero variables.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q64-08ccc6103 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The mathematics is correct. I checked all 7 steps and every new node. Steps 1-2: minimal primes, Tate normalization of each A_i, and finite fraction-field degree and integrality; hypotheses verified. Step 3: the root-compositum node is true. Grouping exponents mod q gives the free basis, F_q=F^{1/q} because K is perfect with |a^{1/q}|=|a|^{1/q}, and g(Z^{p^e}) becomes separable over F^{1/p^e}. Tested on d=0, X^{1/p}, (1+X)^{1/p}, Artin-Schreier and characteristic 0. Steps 4-5: the Galois envelope for n=1, then Stacks 032L (checked in algebra.tex: Noetherian normal domain, finite separable) and lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal give Frac(B_i)=N_i Galois. Step 6 is elementary, with joint injectivity coming from ker j_i=p_i. Step 7: finite-over-affinoid is affinoid (BGR 6.1.1/Conrad 1.2.6(3)) and maps between affinoid algebras are bounded (BGR 6.1.3/1/Conrad 1.2.6(2)); both are true as stated and edge cases were checked. No circular use of the spectral-norm parent. Fault C5: the new node lem-trf-tate-noetherian-normal duplicates the existing lem-trf-tate-integrally-closed (domain and integrally closed, d=0 included, same unit, on base) plus the J=0 case of lem-trf-affinoid-polynomial-closed-point-comparison (Noetherian); the closures were checked and there is no cycle.
